rules.title: AB 325 – Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software that uses competitor data to recommend or influence prices) as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Also makes antitrust pleading easier.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data as part of a restraint of trade or with coercion
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.effective_date_note: Document gives no effective date; chaptered 2025-10-06. 2026-01-01 is the default date for non-urgency California statutes and matches the organizer context (AB 325, 1/1/2026).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm; not limited to housing.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to end consumers.
rules.interaction: Does not impair other antitrust laws.
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act violations; the digest says violations are punishable as a crime.

parsed.doc_summary: Chaptered text of California AB 325 (Stats. 2025, ch. 338), which adds Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 16729 and 16756.1. It bans use or distribution of common pricing algorithms as part of a restraint of trade, or with coercion, and eases Cartwright Act pleading standards.
